checks.name: A1 [deep slope = n*lambda, endpoints] mu(Y)=1-(1+lam*Y)^(-n): mu'(0), mu(0), mu(oo)
checks.reading: the deep slope of the response family is the PRODUCT n*lambda, not n and not lambda separately

checks.name: A2 [OR identification with per-channel slope lam] the family is the OR over n equal channels with engagement p_lam(Y)=1-(1+lam*Y)^(-1), p_lam(0)=0, p_lam'(0)=lam, p_lam(oo)=1
checks.reading: per-channel deep slope is lambda; the composed response slope is then n*lambda = (channel count) x (per-channel slope)

checks.name: A3 [the slope is the product for EVERY completion, at the diagnostic lambda values] for p in {lam*Y/(1+lam*Y), 1-exp(-lam*Y), tanh(lam*Y)}, n in {1,2,3}, lam in {1/2,1,2}: slope of 1-(1-p)^n at 0
checks.measured: 27 (completion, n, lam) triples; all slopes equal n*lam exactly: True
checks.reading: completion-independence of the product slope: mu'(0) = n*lambda is robust to the unknown shape of p (PD01 A1 generalised to per-channel slope lambda)

checks.name: A4 [curvature ratio |c2|/c1^2 = (n+1)/(2n) is lambda-free] Taylor coefficients of mu at 0: c1 = n*lam, c2 = -n(n+1)lam^2/2, c3 = n(n+1)(n+2)lam^3/6
checks.tolerance: exact symbolic; lambda absent from the ratio
checks.reading: the second-order shape coefficient normalized by the slope square depends only on n -- the transition curvature is (in principle) the observable that separates n from lambda; nothing here claims current data measure it

checks.name: A5 [spherical deep matching: a0 = s/(n*lam), kappa = 1/(n*lam)] the deep Poisson first integral is integrated and matched to the a0-line g^2 = a0*g_N
checks.measured: g^2 = G*M*s/(lam*n*r**2) = (s/(n*lam)) * (G M/r^2); a0 = s/(lam*n); kappa = a0/s = 1/(lam*n)
checks.reading: the deep observable is kappa = 1/(n*lambda): only the product enters (equivalently v_flat^4 = G M a0 = G M s/(n*lam))

checks.name: A6 [rank of the deep Jacobian = 1; curvature restores rank 2] J1 = d(n*lam)/d(n,lam); J2 = d(n*lam, |c2|)/d(n,lam)
checks.measured:
J1 = [[lam, n]], rank(J1) = 1, nullspace = [Matrix([
[-n/lam],
[     1]])], J1 . (n, -lam) = Matrix([[0]]); J2 = [[lam, n], [lam**2*n/2 + lam**2*(n + 1)/2, lam*n*(n + 1)]], det(J2) = lam**2*n/2 > 0, rank(J2) = 2
checks.tolerance: exact symbolic ranks; det(J2) = n*lam^2/2 > 0 for n>=1, lam>0
checks.reading: deep data identify the product only (rank 1, kernel direction (dn,dlam)~(n,-lam) preserves n*lam); adding the second-order shape coefficient makes the pair (slope, curvature) identify (n, lam) jointly -- in principle -- via the lambda-free ratio (n+1)/(2n)

checks.name: A7 [the three diagnostic triples are deep-equivalent yet shape-distinct] products n*lambda = 2 at lambda in {1/2,1,2}
checks.measured: deep slopes all 2 (['2', '2', '2']); curvatures |c2| = ['5/2', '3', '4'] (all distinct); ratios ['5/8', '3/4', '1'] (distinct, lambda-free)
checks.reading: ALL three pairs are valid integer-channel configurations with the same deep behaviour: observational preference for (2,1) over (4,1/2) is not a mathematical proof -- deep data cannot distinguish them

checks.name: A8 [both footings carried separately] canonical (kappa=1/2 adopted, product 2) and alternative (fixed-rho_Lambda effective kappa vs fixed-kappa changed density)
checks.tolerance: s_can == 2*a0_can to <1e-12 relative; positivity of the alternative cells
checks.reading: the identifiability theorem is dimensionless: it applies identically to both footings; the canonical product is 2, the fixed-rho_Lambda alternative product is 1/kappa_eff, the fixed-kappa alternative product is 2 again -- in every cell deep data fix only the product

checks.name: B1 [deep limit: slope law with explicit leading correction] mu(Y)/(n*lam*Y) -> 1 and the quadratic remainder equals |c2|*Y^2 at leading order
checks.measured: max |mu/(n lam Y) - 1| at Y=1e-14 = -1.250e-14; remainder/|c2|Y^2 -> 1 (values within 1e-4 of 1 at Y=1e-10)
checks.tolerance: |mu/(n lam Y)-1| < 1e-6 at Y=1e-14; |remainder ratio - 1| < 1e-3 deep in
checks.reading: finite consistency of the exact deep limit and of the leading neglected term -n(n+1)lam^2 Y^2/2 (A4) with its O(Y^3) domain; the deep regime relative error is (n+1)lam*Y/2*(1+O(Y))

checks.name: B2 [Newtonian recovery mu -> 1 with n-dependent tail] g/B -> 1 at large B/s, leading correction (lam*B/s)^(-n)
checks.tolerance: |g/B - 1| < 1e-6 at B/s = 1e18; |slope - (-n)| < 0.02 on the last two resolved rungs
checks.reading: exact Newtonian recovery of the family; the tail exponent is n -- in principle another shape channel, still degenerate with lambda at fixed product whenever only the product is fixed by the deep law

checks.name: B3 [the matched a0-line holds in the first integral] g^2 = a0*g_N with a0 = s/(n*lam) to the stated precision
checks.tolerance: < 1e-6 relative at the deepest rung (mpmath dps=50)
checks.reading: finite consistency of the exact matching identity A5 inside the exact response equation (not just in the slope approximation)

checks.name: C1 [DEEP data fix the product only] fitting n with lambda silently fixed at 1/2, 1, 2 on identical deep data
checks.tolerance: |n_hat*lam - 2|/2 < 1e-3 for all three; every RMS < 1e-3 (deep-plateau level, far below the ~0.11-dex observational scatter; the residual differences between fits are the neglected O(Y^2) completion terms only)
checks.reading: the 'channel count selected by deep data' is exactly product/lambda: n_hat = 4, 2, 1 for lambda = 1/2, 1, 2. The conditional assumption that turns the fitted product into a channel count is lambda = 1 -- the one-scale fraction identity (PD08 steps 1-3, k01 no-go) -- which deep data cannot certify

checks.name: C2 [the same procedure FAILS when the window is not deep: the control is capable of failing] transition-inclusive data with lambda_fixed in {1/2,1,2}
checks.measured: best (lam=1, n=2, the truth) RMS = 0.000e+00; wrong-lambda fits n_hat = [4, 1] with RMS [0.02892696990570519, 0.05445849729435578]; excess over best = truth-exact (abs criterion)
checks.tolerance: wrong-lambda RMS exceeds the best-model RMS by > 10x (or > 1e-3 absolute when the truth model is exact to working precision)
checks.reading: silently fixing lambda while fitting n is valid ONLY on a genuinely deep window; as soon as the window reaches the transition the wrong lambda choices produce residuals orders of magnitude above the plateau, so the control would have FAILED had the deep-law degeneracy not been real. The window condition is an identified, tested assumption

checks.name: C3 [transition-shape observable separates the triples in principle] mu(1) and mu'(1) for the three equal-product configurations
checks.tolerance: pairwise curvature/value separations > 1e-3 (orders above the deep ambiguity level)
checks.reading: a measurement of the response curvature at the transition WOULD break the deep degeneracy and pin n via |c2|/c1^2 = (n+1)/(2n); this states the identifiability criterion, not a claim that current data deliver it

checks.name: D1 [exact identities vs finite consistency, distinguished] what is an exact identity and what is a finite number
checks.measured: EXACT (symbolic): A1-A8 slopes, endpoints, OR identification, Taylor coefficients, ratio (n+1)/2n, spherical matching a0=s/(n lam), kappa=1/(n lam), Jacobian ranks, deep/Newtonian limits, footings algebra. FINITE consistency (mpmath 80 digits): B1-B3 ladders and the C1-C3 fits/separations
checks.reading: the limits are exact symbolic statements; the ladders verify them to finite precision -- a finite consistency check never upgrades to an exact identity by grid density
